page: Microsoft Azure D48as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V45 processors. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provides 48 virtual CPUs mapped across 24 physical cores running at up to 4.5 GHz with dedicated allocation. The system includes 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512 instruction sets, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and advanced bit manipulation extensions. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring remote Premium Storage disks for persistent data persistence, and includes no dedicated hardware GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation reveals strong compute performance across single-threaded and multi-threaded execution. In synthetic testing, stress-ng multi-core reaches 80,204.65, while single-core achieves top-tier results at 3,351.98. In data manipulation workloads, single-threaded gzip compression achieves 36.52 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivers 290.72 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows strong performance with cached reads exceeding 4,482 GB/sec, though large uncached read transfers fall within the middle tier at 157.64 GB/sec. In-memory data store execution demonstrates high throughput, achieving 72.82 million Redis SET operations per second and 57.56 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

The absence of local ephemeral NVMe disks means all input and output depends entirely on remote managed disks, which introduces storage latency tradeoffs for disk-heavy tasks. However, the dedicated AMD core allocation and substantial memory capacity deliver consistent compute density without virtualization overcommit. The machine is well aligned for distributed database backends, static web application clusters, medium-scale container orchestration nodes, in-memory caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D48as_v7 is a general-purpose virtual server powered by 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of system RAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the system integrates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration. It includes no local storage or GPUs, relying on remote network-attached disks for storage requirements. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-threaded compression and strong multi-core processing capabilities, complemented by 72.82 million Redis operations per second and 57.56 GB/sec static web throughput. Its standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation makes it effective for memory-aware computing, microservice backends, in-memory caching layers, and enterprise web serving workloads.
